name: Hub
description: The central controller for an Insteon system. It drives its built-in modem over the local network, and runs scenes, schedules and alerts.

verification.note: Seen on a device: a Hub 2245 reported 0x03/0x33, with modem (PLM) firmware 0xA5 in its Get IM Info reply. Its Hub firmware was 1019, as the Get Info page of Insteon Connect shows it under Firmware, and its Hub software Hub2-V04-20140904.

steps.text: Connect the Hub to the internet and to a power outlet using the Ethernet and power cables provided. Avoid switched outlets and filtered power strips.
Optionally, mount the Hub on a wall: use the template page to drill the mounting holes, then hang the Hub on two screws by aligning its hanger slots and sliding it down.
From your mobile device, download and install the Insteon for Hub app, launch it and follow the on-screen instructions to create an account and set up the Hub.

notes: For the wall mount, the Hub 2245 Owner's Manual gives screw heads about 5/16 inch (8 mm) in diameter.

steps.text: While holding the SET button, reconnect power to the Hub.
When the long beep ends, release the SET button.
steps.expect: Hub double-beeps, and after 30 seconds beeps again

notes: Before a factory reset, delete all devices and scenes from the app (or factory reset all of your devices) and delete your user account.
A Network Reset restores only the default network configuration: tap the SET button three times; the Hub triple-beeps, and after a few seconds it single-beeps.

steps.text: Delete all devices and scenes from the app, or factory reset all of your devices.
From Settings, tap Account, then tap Delete Account. This cannot be undone and erases your home from Insteon's cloud service.

notes: The Hub 2245 Owner's Manual strongly recommends deleting all devices before deleting the account; otherwise network performance degrades. Factory resetting the devices after deleting the account is the alternative.

Seen on a device running Hub firmware 1019: the local interface on port 25105 answers the command pages, such as /3?…=I=3, /buffstatus.xml and /1?XB=M=1, but the settings pages /network.htm and /config.htm don't load, so that device offered no local page for its settings.

Seen on a device running Hub firmware 1019: after an Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 running firmware 0x42 was linked with the Hub as controller, the Hub's controller record for it held Data 1 to 3 as 0x01 0x38 0x42, while the plug had reported 0x02 0x38 0x42 (its category, subcategory and firmware version) in ALL-Linking Completed. Data 2 and 3 matched its subcategory and firmware version, but Data 1 wasn't its category. This was seen with one product only.
